tested_scope.model: 192 finite traces = 4 protocols x 2 current/stale credential states x 3 sink recovery states x 2 prior-effect states x 4 transport/retry traces.
tested_scope.effect_identity: stable effect_id; unsafe means stale generation/incarnation accepted or the same semantic effect applied more than once.
tested_scope.rate_limit_semantics: A rate limit before sink application performs no effect and does not trigger same-run retry; the modeled later retry is a later invocation.
tested_scope.excluded: Byzantine sinks, signature forgery, generic availability of a sink-native anti-rollback primitive, and Part128 repository-incarnation write-time fencing.

protocols.sink_native_nonrollbackable_epoch: Sink atomically checks current generation, current incarnation and permanent effect_id ledger stored in a non-rollbackable sink-native domain that survives reset/rebind.
protocols.signed_certificate_no_sink_floor: A valid signed certificate carries generation/incarnation/effect_id, but the sink has no durable freshness floor; its effect ledger is volatile and is lost on reset/rebind.
protocols.repository_capability_sink_incarnation: A repository-issued capability is signed/bound to sink incarnation and effect_id; the sink compares current incarnation but has no durable generation floor and only a volatile effect ledger.
protocols.fail_closed_until_floor_reestablished: After any sink local-state loss, refuse effects until a current generation/incarnation floor plus effect history is re-established; stable-state operation uses the same currentness/duplicate checks.

diagnostic_slices.signed_certificate_stale_credential: 20/24 unsafe; valid signature without a sink freshness floor does not prove current authority.
diagnostic_slices.signed_certificate_current_credential_af: 8/8 unsafe; after reset/rebind erases the volatile effect ledger, even a current credential can duplicate an already-applied effect.
diagnostic_slices.repository_capability_stale_same_incarna: 8/8 unsafe; incarnation binding alone does not fence an older generation when reset preserves the same incarnation but erases the generation/effect ledger.
diagnostic_slices.repository_capability_stale_same_name_ne: 0/8 unsafe and 8/8 rejected; incarnation binding does fence credentials from the prior incarnation on name reuse.
diagnostic_slices.repository_capability_current_same_incar: 4/4 unsafe; a current bound capability can still replay the same effect after ledger loss.

observed: A sink-native non-rollbackable generation/incarnation/effect ledger produced 0/48 unsafe traces under the modeled recovery/retry scope.
A signed certificate with no sink freshness floor produced 30/48 unsafe traces.
Repository capability plus sink-incarnation binding reduced same-name rebind failures but still produced 21/48 unsafe traces, especially same-incarnation reset and lost effect history.
Fail-closed refusal after local-state loss produced 0/48 unsafe traces but fully blocked 44/48 traces.
observation_vs_inference.inference: Authenticity and incarnation binding are not substitutes for a durable freshness/effect-history floor. Incarnation binding is specifically useful against same-name rebind, but cannot prevent stale-generation or duplicate-effect replay when state loss preserves the incarnation. Generic safety therefore requires at least one recovery domain that cannot roll back the current generation/incarnation/effect history, or fail-closed refusal until such state is re-established.

conditional_safe_mechanisms: fail-closed refusal until an equivalent current floor/history is re-established
phase1_assessment.residual_richer_mode_protected_manual_ex: none in this bounded self-local model
phase1_assessment.quota_zero_rule: Only lightweight repository state transport and local finite modeling were used. Rate-limit interruption checkpoints to a later invocation; no same-run wait/retry, hosted runner, Codespaces, cloud compute, external coordinator, paid credit, artifact/LFS/package quota, or user execution is part of the candidate route.

unresolved_children: No generic zero-cost Chat-native primitive is proven to reconstruct a current sink floor and permanent effect history after complete sink-local loss without importing a second non-rollbackable authority domain.
Part128 repository-incarnation write-time fencing remains unresolved; a repository-issued capability cannot be promoted to generic sink safety while that authority can itself be rebound/rolled back.
Fail-closed refusal is safe in this model but not useful-outcome parity unless a current floor/history can later be re-established without protected/manual execution or finite quota.
continuation: Part131: execute one bounded cross-domain rollback-indistinguishability leaf. Hold Parts127-130 fixed. Model simultaneous rollback/rebind of repository authority and sink-local state after a newer generation/effect has existed, then compare client-carried signed certificates, repository hash-chain/commit identity, sink-local incarnation binding, dual repository+sink witnesses, and fail-closed refusal. Determine whether any zero-cost route can distinguish a legitimately-old world from a rolled-back world without at least one non-rollbackable recovery domain. Include stale credential, same-name reuse, ambiguous committed effect, rate-limit interruption and later retry. Treat impossibility/absence of the needed primitive as an unresolved child, not closure; require zero external hosted coordination, zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota, zero incremental cost, and no richer-mode/protected/manual execution handoff.
